Why go: Pig Island at sunset

Koh Samui's south-west coast faces the sunset, and the best place to watch it is on the water off Thong Krut, looking past the Five Islands (Koh Ha) and the small islands of Koh Tan and Koh Madsum towards the mainland. The sunset tour is the afternoon version of our most popular trip. You snorkel the shallow reef at Koh Tan in the afternoon, spend time with the pigs on Koh Madsum when the light turns warm and the morning boats have gone, then watch the sun go down on the speedboat crossing home before a Thai dinner at a beach restaurant with sea views.

The trip takes 5–6 hours. Pickup is between 13:00 and 14:30, and you are back at your hotel around 19:30, after dark. Sunset on the south-west coast falls at about 17:50–18:10 from October to December, 18:15–18:35 from January to May, 18:35–18:45 from June to August and around 18:20 in September, and the itinerary is timed around it. Clouds can hide the sun on any day, especially in the rainy months of October to December, but the evening light over the islands is usually worth it anyway.

Compared with the morning speedboat tour (1,450 THB, 4–5 hours), the sunset trip costs 100 THB more, runs later, swaps lunch for dinner and adds the sunset crossing. The beaches are often quieter in the late afternoon, and the heat has dropped. If you would rather have a full day with lunch on Koh Tan, take the longtail tour instead.

Who this tour is for

  • Couples and families who want the pigs, a swim and a sunset in one easy afternoon.
  • Anyone who prefers a slow morning: there is no early start.
  • Photographers: golden light on the white sand of Koh Madsum, then the sunset from the water.
  • Travellers in November and early December, when the trip runs as normal while Ang Thong is closed.

Who should choose another tour

  • Want lunch instead of dinner, or the cheapest option: the morning speedboat tour.
  • Want a longer, slower day: the small-group longtail.
  • Want a private sunset: the private longtail (afternoon start, 5,950 THB per boat), or see sunset cruises for catamarans and yachts.
  • Pregnant or with back or neck problems: it is a speedboat, which bounces on choppy water; choose the longtail and check with your doctor.
  • Very young children who sleep early: the return is after dark; the morning trip is easier.

What to bring

  • A light layer for the ride home: it gets cool on the water after sunset.
  • Insect repellent for dinner on the beach.
  • Swimwear, a towel and a change of clothes.
  • Reef-safe sunscreen, a hat and sunglasses for the afternoon.
  • A dry bag or phone pouch, and a charged phone or camera for the sunset.
  • Cash in small notes for drinks, snacks and any island fee not covered by your booking.

Good to know

  • Sea by month: January to September is best, with February to April calmest. October to December brings showers most days, and some afternoons are cloudy. The trip runs every day of the year when the sea is safe. If we cancel for weather, you choose a full refund or a new date.
  • After dark: the last part of the trip is in twilight or darkness. Life jackets are worn on the boat, and children wear them at all times.
  • Seasickness: afternoon wind can make the water a little choppier than in the morning. Sit towards the back.
  • Dinner: a Thai dinner, mild unless you ask for spice. Tell us about vegetarian, halal or allergy needs when you book.
  • Mobility: boarding may involve stepping down from a pier or wading at the beach. There are no climbs unless you choose the short viewpoint walk on Koh Madsum.
  • The pigs: watch and photograph them, let them come to you, and don't chase, lift or feed them junk food.
  • Drones: registered drones only (CAAT and NBTC); ask the captain first and never fly over the animals or other guests.
  • Children: children aged 3–11 pay the child price and infants up to 2 travel free.

Pickup and meeting point

Minibus transfers to Thong Krut harbour are included from the main areas of Koh Samui: Chaweng, Lamai, Bophut, Maenam, Choeng Mon, Bang Rak and Plai Laem. Remote areas cost 400 THB per person return; the booking card shows any surcharge for your area. Pickup is between 13:00 and 14:30, and we send your exact time by 18:00 the day before. If the minibus can't reach your road, we send a nearby meeting point with a map pin. You can also meet the group at Thong Krut pier; message us on WhatsApp first.
